subject: Firebreak: Runway slippage investigation for ACME eval — immediate mitigation
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Ellis <jordan.ellis@acme-corp.com>, acme-pm@acme-corp.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 4 Jun 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Firebreak: Runway slippage investigation for ACME eval — immediate mitigation

Jordan / ACME team —

Thanks for the heads up on the scheduling noise this morning. I went through the shared evaluation calendar and the MAP milestones and I can see two sources of misalignment that could push the close date: (1) the security questionnaire turnaround that was scoped for next week, and (2) a compressed internal test window on your side that overlaps our planned canary.

Immediate asks:
- Jordan: can you confirm whether the security questionnaire is the blocker or if it's the internal test timing? If it's the questionnaire, any chance we get interim answers for the high-risk items by EOD Friday?
- Marissa / Ben: please start a short risk snapshot (attached) and a proposed rebaseline for the MAP with two recovery lanes (fast/medium). I want a one-page comms note for ACME leadership by tomorrow noon.

My goal: prevent a hard slip by using a firebreak — temporary scope reduction for the canary + targeted security evidence handoff. If that fails, we escalate to a one-week contingency hold and trigger the reserved capacity fallbacks.

Attachments: runway_risk_snapshot_20250604.pdf

Thanks,
Naomi Feldman
Head of Sales Operations | Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0192

--
Redwood Inference — Production-first inference platform
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Ellis <jordan.ellis@acme-corp.com>, acme-pm@acme-corp.com
Date: Thu, 5 Jun 2025 08:26:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Firebreak: Runway slippage investigation for ACME eval — immediate mitigation

Naomi / team —

Thanks — I reviewed the MAP and the gating checklist. Quick findings (summary):
- Security questionnaire: two high-priority items (data retention and audit logs) outstanding; ACME legal flagged an additional evidence request around KMS integration. Jordan, if you can provide the KMS diagram + retention doc by EOD Friday we can mark those as "in evidence" and proceed with a limited canary.
- Internal test window: ACME's QA lead moved the UAT by 3 days; that's causing overlap with our final canary. Proposal: shift only the external-facing acceptance test by 48 hours and run the internal canary on the original cadence with a scoped dataset (reduced tokens / feature flags).

I attached a rebaseline workbook with two lanes:
- Lane A (fast): limited canary + partial QA shift — delta: +2 days to close, minimal revenue impact.
- Lane B (safe): full QA shift + complete evidence handoff — delta: +7 days, triggers reserved-capacity fallback.

I'll prepare the one-pager for leadership and flag the recommended next steps.

Attachments: proposed_map_rebaseline_20250605.xlsx

—Marissa
Marissa Cole | Sr. Account Executive, Enterprise Sales
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 (650) 555-0123
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Jordan Ellis <jordan.ellis@acme-corp.com>
Date: Thu, 5 Jun 2025 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Firebreak: Runway slippage investigation for ACME eval — immediate mitigation

Marissa / Naomi —

Adding two practical mitigations from ops:
1) Can we run the canary on a dedicated sandbox node in our us-west region for 24 hours (isolated, lower scale) to validate the happy path without waiting on full QA? Ops can spin this up same-day if we greenlight.
2) If ACME can accept a scoped feature flag (turn off model caching for the canary), that reduces the KV-cache incompatibility risk that came up in the last eval.

If both are acceptable, Lane A becomes much more likely. I'll coordinate provisioning and will post a short status once the sandbox is ready.

—Ben
Ben Carter | Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com
From: Jordan Ellis <jordan.ellis@acme-corp.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: acme-pm@acme-corp.com, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 6 Jun 2025 09:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Firebreak: Runway slippage investigation for ACME eval — immediate mitigation

Naomi / Marissa / Ben —

Thanks for the quick triage. To confirm: the blocker is primarily the legal evidence around KMS and retention. We can accelerate by providing the KMS diagram today and partial answers to the retention questions by Friday EOD. The QA lead also confirmed a 48-hour buffer is feasible if the sandbox can validate the external flow.

We agree to Lane A (fast) provided Redwood can: (1) provision the sandbox today and (2) scope the canary to the reduced dataset + feature flag. If both green, we keep the close as planned with a +2 day slippage window.

I'll share the KMS diagram in a follow-up email and loop my legal lead if anything else is needed.

—Jordan
Jordan Ellis | Senior Product Manager, ACME Corporation
jordan.ellis@acme-corp.com | +1 (617) 555-0099
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Date: Fri, 6 Jun 2025 17:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Firebreak: Runway slippage investigation for ACME eval — immediate mitigation

Team —

Good news: ops confirmed sandbox provisioning and Ben validated the reduced-feature flag path. Jordan to deliver KMS diagram by EOD; Marissa, please finalize the MAP rebaseline doc (Lane A as canonical, Lane B as contingency) and circulate the one-page to ACME leadership. I will: (a) open an escalation channel with the reserved-capacity team (pre-approve the +7 day fallback), and (b) schedule a 30-min alignment call Monday to lock down final acceptance criteria.

Action tracker (who/what/when):
- Jordan: KMS diagram and retention interim answers — due Fri 6pm PT (ACME)
- Ben: sandbox ready and test summary — due Fri 6pm PT (Redwood Ops)
- Marissa: one-page MAP rebaseline and comms to ACME leadership — due Mon 9am PT (Redwood Sales)
- Naomi: escalation channel + reserved-capacity pre-approval — done by Mon 9am PT

If Lane A holds, we expect a +2 day delta and no revenue impact. If not, we will enact Lane B and notify finance/procurement to start the procurement bridge. I'll post the final status after Monday's call.

Thanks all — pragmatic and fast on this saved the close.

Naomi Feldman
Head of Sales Operations | Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.com
